Snapcards — engineering design

Compiled from journal.html#initial-brief by the studio team, onto the mecha cluster, the omnishell terminal, the sayt loop, and the bayt build graph · design tokens: DESIGN.md (Editorial Press).

Overview

Snapcards is a cultural children’s publishing and flashcard press in six languages (en, pt, es, ja, he, ar, with full RTL layout for Hebrew and Arabic). Readers browse curated and community-authored specimen decks, study cards on a tactile desk with phonetic pronunciation and cultural bento notes, synthesize new decks across a three-tier AI press, and lay out printable A4 or Letter sheets with crop marks and fold guides.

Curated and user-generated decks (CardSet, Flashcard) take the offline path so the catalogue syncs across devices while remaining playable without a connection, as do each device's two text slots (GenerationDraft), partitioned by the key the device holds in Device. The /generate form is the browser's own GenerationForm, never synced. In-tab study state (PlaySession), print sheet geometry (PrintConfig), and per-locale projections (LocalizedDeck, LocalizedCard) live in tab tables folded by the mecha deck_press machine and locale handlers. Deck synthesis spans three tiers: in-browser WebGPU worker drafting via the ai-browser agent unit memoized into BrowserDraft, cluster-side text effects (smollm3-draft cheap and heavy-draft heavy) orchestrated by GenerationMachine, whose outcomes fan out through the card-art-fan-out hatch to one CardArt row per card and level, each drawn by its own illustrate-card effect; the deck-level drain counts them into DeckLevel, which settles the deck.

effect smollm3-draft → ai text (cheap) · idempotent delivery exactly-once · tsbifrost AI gateway text drafting is deterministic for a given (id, topic, locale, region) key; the id names the device's slot, so two devices never share a key

effect heavy-draft → ai text (heavy) · idempotent delivery exactly-once · tsbifrost AI gateway heavy text drafting is deterministic for a given (id, topic, locale, region) key; the id names the device's slot, so two devices never share a key

SQL hatch card-art-fan-out · delivery unspecified · a text level's outcome becomes one CardArt row per card, and its words the cards' words; a relational effect writes one row

SQL hatch deck-advance · delivery unspecified · the chart source adapter observes relational facts and dispatches events

the platform’s columns

created_by, updated_by → app_user, stamped by the platform on every write; not the author’s.

machine CardArtMachine · status level externaldelivery exactly-once

effect illustrate-card → ai image (heavy) · idempotent · tsbifrost AI gateway image synthesis is deterministic per (id, run, redraws) key: the level picks the tier, the position and the redraw the seed, and the reader's words are translated by the cheap text tier first

One card's picture at one level (2 cheap, 3 heavy), fanned out from a settled text level. CardArtMachine holds it waiting until its own card's level 2 settles, then pending invokes illustrate-card keyed by the row and its run; the outcome is drawn (written to the flashcard's back), failed with the provider's refusal, or unknown once attempts ran out.

machine DeckProgressMachine · status level replicateddelivery exactly-once

Where a deck is across its two drawn levels, one row per deck and run. Its DeckProgressMachine names every combination the levels can be in: level 2 drawing, both drawing, level 2 settled with its outcome, level 3 drawing after it, and the deck's end, done when every card was drawn at both levels, failed when none was, partial otherwise. The deck-level drain picks the state from the counts and the machine refuses a move the levels cannot make. The form settles from it, the progress bar follows it, and the generate screen's Cortex chart hears each of its states as a signal.

deck-level — drain

Recomputes every deck's level counts from card_art over the cards that still exist, writing only rows that moved; a drain because the edge and the page run no stream, and a streamed drain is the maintainer every target runs.

favorite-recount — cdc

The absolute count of the event's own deck, never a delta, with the newest favourite it read as its watermark; in the browser a fold over the reader's own rows above that watermark, so a favourite shows at once.

favorite-count — cdc

The acting reader's pair: whether the total its read produced included them.

deck-favorites — drain

On the edge, where no stream runs, keeps what the two pipelines above keep in a container (022_deck_favorites.sql).

deck-cover — cdc

The event's own deck's cover, its first card's art by id, beside its count, so a library card reads one row; the count's columns stay the recount's. The browser tier keeps no fold for it.

deck-covers — drain

On the edge, keeps what deck-cover keeps in a container (migrations/20261108_deck_cover.sql).

Browse cultural card sets, filter by category and locale, search by title or region, toggle favorites, and launch a study desk or print studio session.

Host-DOM hatch print-checkout · delivery unspecified · Draws each card's 6×4 in artwork on a canvas and uploads it, opens Checkout from the order row and shows its state; for a print shop, composes one A6 page per face for the browser's print dialog; Pages simulates the external services.

The physical printing press. Its first control is the vendor. Print shop is free and needs no server: it downloads a PDF of one A6 face per page, with bleed and page boxes, and gives the reader the text to hand the shop. Print at home imposes cards onto A4 or Letter sheets in fold, duplex, 2x2, or 3x3 grids with crop marks and cutting guides. Prodigi prints and posts one 6×4 in postcard per card: the other controls lock with their reason, stock is the one choice, and the preview shows each card's front and back.

About (/about)

Host-DOM hatch window-print · delivery unspecified · calls window.print() when the user clicks #btn-window-print

The press's front page, for readers and for search engines: what Snapcards makes and how, then a call to visit its publisher, Bonisoft, and its privacy policy. It reads no rows, so its document is written per locale at build. The rail links to it, after the press's own screens.

Picture Flashcards for Kids (/kids)

A search ad's landing page for parents of young children: one headline on picture vocabulary flashcards, three benefits (any topic illustrated, the child's own pace, five languages), a fan of animal word cards, Create as the one way in and the library beside it. It reads no rows, so its document is written per locale at build; the strip does not list it.

Classroom Flashcards (/teachers)

A search ad's landing page for teachers: a deck per lesson, printed with cut lines at school or at a shop, shared by its link. The solar-system cards sit on a cut sheet; Create is the one way in and the library beside it. It reads no rows, so its document is written per locale at build; the strip does not list it.

Printed Picture Cards (/printed)

A search ad's landing page for printed cards delivered: the spiral flip-deck Brazil receives, the postcards the other print countries receive, and the countries named exactly as the order's country check allows. Create is the one way in and the library beside it. It reads no rows, so its document is written per locale at build; the strip does not list it.

Decisions

A card is deleted by two taps on the same button

The 🗑 on a card of a deck this tab generated is one button. The first tap arms it: it turns into a red "Apagar?" button, localized, and a second tap within about four seconds deletes the card; otherwise it reverts to 🗑. There is no confirmation box and no extra text. The arming is a terminal chart over a tab row, card_delete, one per card: idle → armed on a click, armed → idle after 4000 ms on the terminal's clock, armed → confirmed on the second click. The revert is the chart's after, not CSS: a CSS clock is rejected by omnishell (reduced motion and background tabs run it at the wrong speed, and ?clock=manual cannot hold it), and a hand-written timer has no place in a handler. The button keeps its focus across both taps, so a keyboard reader presses it twice, and its name moves from "Apagar carta" to "Apagar?" inside a polite live region, which a screen reader announces.

A confirmed row is an intent row. create_set, seated on card_delete with data-on-mutation, applies it as before: owned decks only, never the deck's last card, the deck's count and the session's position follow. A refused intent drops the row, which returns the button to 🗑.

A card is edited in a bottom sheet that redraws its level 3

A ✏️ on the card in view (explore and the card route, owned decks only, where the delete control shows) opens a sheet the app styles, a popover like #draft-loc-menu: the card's current image, one field "Detalhes desta imagem", a "Gerar de novo" button and a "Pronto" button that closes it. "Gerar de novo" is a form update of the card's Flashcard row: its description and redraw: drawing. CardRedrawMachine takes settled → drawing only while the card's level-3 CardArt row has settled, and that transition restarts the row as a new run of the effect: redraws grows by one, which is part of illustrate-card's key and of its seed, so the same text twice is still a new drawing. The row carries the reader's description; drawn, the image replaces the card's art, and either outcome settles the card back. The sheet's bar reads the row's state with colour alone, as the generation bars do, and a refused or unanswered drawing shows the no-art frame in the sheet while the card keeps the art it had. The reader may redraw again as soon as it settles.

Rejected: a new request entity beside the card (a second row to keep in step with the card it describes), and a new deck run for one card (it would move DeckLevel's run and make the tab read the deck's text as unsettled).

A picture is drawn from the reader's words, for the deck's audience

The text levels once wrote each card an English picture description and a reader-facing one; the first was the image prompt and the second prefilled the edit sheet, so model prose the reader never wrote decided what was drawn. They now write the cards' words alone, and the sheet starts empty. illustrate-card asks for Subject: a single <word>. Context: <title>; <details>. from the card's word and the deck's title, details and custom audience, with a redraw's description, then the audience's style and a white background. Level 3 draws on Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image from the words as written: Phoenix drew a paca as an alpaca and a giant anteater as a mongoose whatever the prompt said. Level 2's model reads English alone, so the cheap text tier translates the words there, and the reader's word stays beside its translation. The trials and the rejected options are in the archived record docs/archive/2026-10-31-image-prompt.md. No prompt is seeded with examples drawn from a deck a test generates.

A deck is created from a title and optional details

The form has two fields. "Título da coleção" is short and becomes the deck's name (topic on the draft, name on the CardSet). "Detalhes (opcional)" refines the text effects' prompt for every card and is never shown as the title; it rides the draft and the deck (details), so a level started from the deck's rows asks the same thing.

The /generate preview shows the deck being generated

The preview bound play_session, which create_set would not move while a generation was unsettled, so it went on showing a deck explored before. It now binds the form's row draft (generation_form): its set_id and that deck's cards, showing the session's card only when the session is on that deck and the deck's first card otherwise. The session-healing code that moved the session to the generated deck is gone.

Generation continues with the browser closed

Query actors observe card, draft and artwork facts and deliver events to durable Cortex charts in the same transaction. The form attaches to its deck's progress while the screen is open; it does not own the server work.

The form and the text slots are the device's

The form was one public row every visitor shared with the slots beside it: a fresh browser showed another reader's title and details, and a second writer reverted a reader's card count. The unsent form is now the browser's GenerationForm, durability device, never synced, and its attached chart observes the deck's DeckProgress row. It was the tab's at first, and a reload mid-generation then forgot the deck it was generating while the server went on drawing it; the tabs of one browser now share the form, which is the reader's one draft whichever tab shows it. The server's rows stay server-side so a deck finishes with the tab closed, partitioned by a device key: create_set mints it once from two of the terminal's draws into Device, with the device's two slots <key>:draft-cheap and <key>:draft-heavy, and a deck names its device in card_set.device. The deck's id ends in the key too: a title alone made two devices titling a deck alike write one deck. Rejected: a server form row per reader (it would sync typed text only this browser needs), keying the form by tab (a reload loses it), and keying the slots by tab (a deck's slots must outlive the tab that asked).

A deck is its owner's; a favourite each reader's; a translation everyone's

Which decks were a reader's lived in a tab-only list, so a reload, a new tab or a pasted link made every deck someone else's and hid its ✏️ from its own author, while the server let anyone write any deck: card_set and flashcard were public writes, and one card_set.favorite field was every visitor's favourite. A deck and its cards now carry owner, the signed-in reader (a guest is one, with an id the server minted), stamped by auth_uid(); anyone reads them and only the owner writes them (020_owner_writes.sql, since #Access has no such mode). The browser asks the same question of Me, the reader's one visible row. A favourite is each reader's own Favorite, counted in DeckStats, as realworld counts an article's. Translations, which every reader wrote into the cards' hints, are DeckTranslation and CardTranslation, a cache any reader writes, so reading someone else's deck in another language writes nothing of theirs. Promoting a guest keeps the person's id, so their decks stay theirs. Rejected: ownership by device key (the deck already names it, but a person on a second browser would own nothing), and keeping the tab's list in device storage (still one browser's, and the server would go on accepting anyone's writes).

Escape hatches

window-print calls the browser's print dialog; card-art-fan-out writes one art row per card, and generation-slot-bootstrap restores a device slot, and deck-advance dispatches the source facts. ai-browser runs a model in a worker. Each is where replay stops.

Capabilities, Units & Handlers

window-print (Host-DOM Hatch)

Invokes window.print() when the reader clicks #btn-window-print in the Print Studio.

Retained RLS baseline

The original bootstrap bytes stay fixed so an existing installation accepts its forward migration.

card-art-fan-out (SQL Hatch)

A settled text level becomes one CardArt row per card and the cards' words; a relational effect writes one row.

deck-advance (SQL Hatch)

Reconciles generation facts and delivers events to their durable charts in the caller's transaction.

Generation slot recovery (SQL Hatch)

An accepted deck restores its device's missing worker slot; curated decks create no worker rows.

ai-browser (Vendored Agent Unit)

Runs in-browser WebGPU/WASM topic drafting inside an isolated worker agent, writing memoized answers into BrowserDraft.

Generation input

Each Create retains the form input it accepted while earlier requests finish.

Value is

A chart's guard: the arrow for what a control holds, as typed.

Retained generation

A saved form adopts the run of its own deck when it predates run tracking.

Row is

A chart's guard: an always arrow for a column a fold wrote.

Tab fill

A chart's guard: an unmodified Tab on an empty field takes its ghost value.

Count step

A chart's assign: the card count an arrow steps or the field takes typed, held to 1 to 20; the presets assign their literal.

is_key

A keydown guard: whether the key is the one the arrow answers to.

delivery_address_q

The postal fields as one question, taken when a field is committed rather than while the reader types.

delivery_submitted

The free text, copied to the search question only when the reader presses Enter or the search button.

delivery_found

A search answer becomes the list of places the checkout offers, only while the reader still asks that search.

delivery_offers

A fold over the draft and the place memo: the street near the pin is offered only where it is not the street in the fields, and the fields' street only where it lies more than 50 m from the pin; it is weighed again whenever either changes.

delivery_pin

The reader's position or the map's centre becomes the pin; the free text and the postal fields are left as they are.

delivery_accept

An offer the reader applies writes the pin or the postal fields it names and records itself in the order's applied suggestions; it never writes the free text, recipient, unit line or instructions.

delivery-map — the delivery map, in a frame

MapLibre 5.24.0 over OpenFreeMap tiles behind an opaque origin, with a pin the reader moves only by taking it, and a toggle for their own position, asked only on a click under the frame's delegated geolocation grant and turned off by an empty pin. It raises the pin and nothing else.

geocoder — OpenStreetMap Nominatim, under the app's policy

A worker answering search, address and reverse questions once each into the place memo. Nominatim's policy holds it to one request a second for the whole origin and forbids asking while the reader types, so a search is asked only when submitted.

print-payment — embedded Checkout, in the payments subdomain realm

Stripe Checkout embedded in a frame on the payments subdomain under the frame's delegated payment grant, raising the checkout outcome when the session completes or is cancelled.

Print checkout

Opens only under the Prodigi vendor; Print at home has no checkout. The delivery section collects free text, an optional pin and postal fields as independent statements, and the order freezes all three. Prodigi posts to the postal fields, so recipient, street, city, postal code and country are required: payment stays disabled until they are complete and the service has quoted them, as item, shipping and total. The hatch holds that quote in memory and carries it signed; the chart and the delivery row hold everything the reader chose. Preparing the postcards renders each card as one 3708×1263 image of both faces in the browser, committed atomically with the order. Checkout, payment pending, paid, declined, vendor accepted, shipped and vendor failure are visible states in its modal order review. Escape and the close control return focus to the studio. Pages labels every simulated payment and sends no mail. Live checkout never falls back to simulation.

the platform’s columns

created_by, updated_by → app_user, stamped by the platform on every write; not the author’s.

machine PrintOrderMachine · status level externaldelivery exactly-once · at-least-once

effect print-quote → the origin in PRODIGI_ORIGIN · idempotent delivery exactly-once · A quote changes nothing at Prodigi

effect print-quote-br → https://api.cloudprinter.com · idempotent delivery exactly-once · A domestic Brazil quote changes nothing at Cloudprinter

effect print-fx → https://api.stripe.com · idempotent delivery exactly-once · Stripe answers a repeated Idempotency-Key with the quote it made

effect print-session → https://api.stripe.com · idempotent delivery exactly-once · Stripe answers a repeated Idempotency-Key with the session it made, and the print files are rebuilt from the same content keys

effect print-check → https://api.stripe.com · idempotent delivery exactly-once · A read of the session

effect print-confirm → https://api.cloudflare.com · not idempotent · re-entry repeat delivery at-least-once · Immediate buyer order confirmation before printer placement; returns Message-ID for threading

effect print-place → the origin in PRODIGI_ORIGIN · idempotent delivery exactly-once · A repeated idempotencyKey answers AlreadyExists with the first order, ignoring a changed body (sandbox, 2026-11-05)

effect print-place-br → https://api.cloudprinter.com · idempotent delivery exactly-once · CloudCore enforces unique order reference (409 on repeat), reconciled via /orders/info

effect print-record → https://api.cloudflare.com · not idempotent · re-entry repeat delivery at-least-once · Replies in the buyer's confirmation thread once the printer accepts, and archives the operator record

effect print-status → the origin in PRODIGI_ORIGIN · idempotent delivery exactly-once · A read of the order

effect print-status-br → https://api.cloudprinter.com · idempotent delivery exactly-once · A read of the Cloudprinter order

effect print-shipped → https://api.cloudflare.com · not idempotent · re-entry repeat delivery at-least-once · Replies in the buyer's confirmation thread with carrier and tracking details once shipped

effect print-alert → https://api.cloudflare.com · not idempotent · re-entry repeat delivery at-least-once · A second alert costs a glance, and a lost one leaves a paid order unseen

One order of printed cards. An order is a machine over a row: every call out is an external effect, so the ledger holds what was asked and how a repeat is answered. A webhook only names the row to re-check, and Stripe's own read of a matching session marks it paid, and a clock asks it again while a payment is unsettled. Each country pays in its own currency, priced from Prodigi's USD cost through a Stripe FX quote to the same BRL received. Payment and delivery are separate: a failed email never asks the buyer to pay again. Column grants keep the price and the payment out of a browser's reach.

checkout-simulator (container)

Stripe Checkout for the compose stack: its API, its hosted page, and webhooks to the door.

prodigi-simulator (container)

Prodigi for the compose stack: artwork fetched through the door as a lab would, callbacks to the door.

cloudprinter-simulator (container)

Cloudprinter CloudCore for the compose stack: cover and book PDFs fetched through the door, CloudSignal webhooks to the door.

mail-simulator (container)

Cloudflare's Email Sending API for the compose stack, handed to Mailpit.
